answer: Laser-induced incandescence counters Sybil attacks by optically probing soot micro-particles. An agent pulses a focal laser to heat an airborne particle into a glowing ember, measuring pyrometric decay as a convective plume dissipates heat. Attackers must provision discrete vacuum chambers and high-speed photodetectors per identity, establishing a physical haven against software spoofing. However, repeated vaporization shifts particle mass over time, causing false rejections.
